basis: Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy; encephalopathy or leukodystrophy affects >30% across major nuclear forms. Cardiomyopathy varies by subtype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct encephalopathy, Leigh disease or leukodystrophy occurs in >30% across the major nuclear forms.

basis: Adrenal medullary endocrine tumor; hypertension occurs in ~80-90% but does not itself establish direct cardiovascular injury. Cardiomyopathy occurs in <30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: common catecholamine-mediated hypertension (~80-90%) does not establish direct cardiovascular damage; cardiomyopathy occurs in <30%.

basis: Traumatic spinal cord damage; bladder sphincter dysfunction (30-79%) reflects neural injury, with neurogenic bladder separately diagnosed. Vertebral fractures occur in 5-29%.

decisions.renal: none: sphincter dysfunction (30-79%) results from neural injury; direct urinary tract damage is not established, and neurogenic bladder is separately diagnosed.

basis: Developmental motor impairment and hypotonia span the umbrella. Major thoracic skeletal defects characterize Kagami-Ogata; small hands and feet alone do not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: major structural skeletal disease is subtype-dependent; growth restriction and small extremities do not establish common locomotor damage across the umbrella.

basis: Defective albumin/IgG recycling causes hypercatabolism and immunodeficiency. Bronchiectasis (2/2) is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (2/2) is secondary structural disease following recurrent infections, rather than direct pulmonary injury from the protein-recycling defect.

basis: CD81 antibody deficiency; immune-complex nephritis/CKD and autoimmune thrombocytopenia, each reported in 1/1, are separately diagnosed autoimmune complications.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune thrombocytopenia (1/1 reported patient) is a separately diagnosed autoimmune complication.
decisions.renal: none: immune-complex nephritis and resulting CKD (1/1 reported patient) constitute separately diagnosed renal disease complicating antibody deficiency.

basis: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes profound hypoglycemia; persistent hypoglycemic neurodevelopmental injury affects roughly 30-50% in severe congenital hyperinsulinism.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe, refractory congenital hyperinsulinism causes direct hypoglycemic brain injury with persistent developmental impairment in roughly 30-50%.

basis: Defining metabolic acidosis occurs in 80-99%; common intoxication signs do not establish neural damage. Encephalopathy occurs in 1-4%, renal insufficiency in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none: common ataxia/confusion/drowsiness are acute intoxication signs; damaging encephalopathy or cerebral edema is reported in only 1-4%.

basis: Scleritis-associated deep stromal keratitis causes corneal sclerosis and is generally an immune-mediated ocular inflammatory process.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: sclerosing keratitis associated with anterior scleritis is generally immune-mediated, including idiopathic noninfectious cases.

basis: Basilar arterial occlusion is vascular disease; resulting cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication and is not required by this concept.

decisions.neurologic: none: brain infarction commonly accompanies symptomatic occlusion but is a separately diagnosed disease; arterial occlusion alone does not establish cerebral injury.
